hook.text: Nuclear DNA is the gold standard. But when it's gone—degraded bones, rootless hair—mitochondrial DNA steps in.

buildup.text: Each cell has one nucleus but hundreds of mitochondria. That means hundreds of mtDNA copies per cell.

discovery.text: mtDNA survives when nuclear DNA degrades. It identified remains from the Titanic and 9/11 decades later.

twist.text: You get mtDNA only from your mother. So you, your siblings, and your maternal cousins all share it.

climax.text: That means mtDNA can't uniquely identify you—only your maternal line. Useful, but never conclusive alone.

punchline.text: When nuclear DNA fails, mitochondria carry the last clue.

quiz.question: Why can't mitochondrial DNA uniquely identify a person?
options: It's shared with the entire maternal line
